# Phase One — Sitewide UI Revelation

The Awtsmoos renews every pixel and pathway from nothing in each instant;
Awtsmoos.com is remembered while every unfinished control receives one coherent garment.

## Mission

Audit the entire Geelooy website and eliminate visually unowned native controls, incomplete styling, viewport escape, accidental overlap, z-index mistakes, and inconsistent interaction states.

## Evidence from the supplied screenshots

- Social Hub renders native browser `<audio controls>` chrome inside otherwise custom message cards.
- The message composer textarea/input zone is visually only partially integrated into the surrounding glass/futuristic language.
- Fixed bottom composition and the browser-height viewport create a risk of content being hidden behind the composer/dock.
- The home surface has large zones where layout hierarchy is weak compared with the otherwise strong constellation UI.
- Chips and status controls are visually stronger than adjacent plain/form regions, producing a mixed-design-system effect.

## Sitewide failure contract

A route fails the audit when any of these are observed:

- browser-native audio/video/form controls visibly escape the page design;
- input, textarea, select, label, progress, meter or file controls lack intentional styling;
- interactive elements lack `:hover`, `:active`, `:focus-visible`, disabled, or reduced-motion behavior where relevant;
- controls or menus overflow the viewport or depend on document horizontal scrolling;
- fixed/sticky overlays collide with one another or hide actionable content;
- raw z-index values form an unstructured stacking war;
- a page mixes unrelated visual systems because shared selectors leak globally;
- half-styled regions or accidental default typography remain;
- mobile targets are too small or visually clipped;
- short-height viewports lose access to primary actions;
- dialogs/drawers/menus lack internal scrolling and viewport bounds;
- native media surfaces are not wrapped by a custom accessible control layer.

## Audit dimensions

1. Route census: every HTML/page entry under root, apps, games, social, admin/tool surfaces.
2. Native-element census: audio, video, input, textarea, select, button, label, progress, meter, details, dialog, file controls.
3. CSS ownership census: unscoped selectors, bare element selectors, wildcard selectors, z-indexes, fixed/sticky layers.
4. Runtime geometry: horizontal overflow, viewport escape, clipped controls, overlap, fixed-layer collisions.
5. Interaction states: hover, active, focus-visible, disabled, reduced motion.
6. Visual completeness: typography, fields, cards, media, empty states, loading/error states.
7. Mobile-first acceptance: 390x844, 320x568, and short-height cases.

## Immediate priority order

1. Social Hub / private messages because the supplied evidence proves active visible defects.
2. Shared social components if those defects are reused across multiple social routes.
3. High-traffic apps/games with native controls.
4. Remaining public apps and games.
5. Tool/admin/utility pages.
6. Whole-site regression gate so plain elements cannot silently return.

## Preservation law

Do not create a global stylesheet that reaches into unrelated pages. Every remediation must be scoped beneath the owning page/application root or implemented through an explicitly imported reusable component module whose selectors remain namespaced.
